title: The QA role on the team: not the guardian of "you cannot ship"

videos.script: Picture the tester as a guard at a door. Nothing ships until QA says it may. {{guard}} It sounds responsible. Watch what it does to a team. {{watch}} Developers check less, because someone downstream will check everything. {{less}} Work arrives at the end, all at once, when there is least time to look. {{late}} Reports turn into arguments. And when a defect escapes anyway, the gate turns out to have provided one thing. Someone to blame. {{blame}} This lesson argues for a different job. The tester gives information, and the person who owns the product decides. {{information}} What is known, what it costs, what was not tested, and what would reduce the risk. {{four}} It also covers the cases where information is not enough. The law, people's safety, and their data. {{hard}} And it ends with a simple test. When a developer is unsure, do they send it to QA, or ask Lia what she would try? {{end}}
